newsitem.title: CROATIA: Blaze on Croat holiday isle advances towards towns.
newsitem.headline: Blaze on Croat holiday isle advances towards towns.

text.p: Over 1,000 Croatian firemen fought a losing battle with a huge blaze on Hvar island on Wednesday as it advanced for the third day running to threaten more towns on the popular Adriatic resort.

The flames, pushed on by strong winds, have destroyed some 3,000 hectares (7,400 acres) of pine forests, vineyards, farming fields and olive groves on the idyllic sunspot since they broke out around midday on Monday, state news agency HINA said.

Local authorities, who declared a state of emergency on Tuesday, said the fire was threatening more villages while their efforts were being hampered by the breakdown of two of the three planes used in the operation. The army was also on hand, HINA said.
"The fire has now spread across the centre of the island through dense pine forests to the eastern part. It is now getting closer to the villages in the east," a Hvar police official said.
"Some 1,050 firemen from all over Croatia are now fighting the fire, with the help of two helicopters and only one plane since the two other ones broke down yesterday."

The policeman said the fire was roughly 18 km east of the historic town of Hvar and some three km south from Stari Grad. The blaze reached the ferry port near Stari Grad on Monday but was brought under control, he said.
On Monday the northern 'Tramuntana' wind spread the fire from the centre, where it started, towards the south of the island, but the wind direction shifted to south-westerly on Tuesday.
"The westerly 'Mistral' wind is still blowing, and it is even stronger than it was yesterday," the policeman said.
Croatian media said several firefighters had sustained minor injuries in the most serious fire the island has seen in years.
